thread:
pagerbot: PAGER - HIGH severity: auth-service detected token replay spike from multiple IPs (src ASN 396982). Alerting oncall.
maya: seeing the page, I'm on it. what's the signal?
pagerbot: detections: >5000 identical jti values seen in 3m across 5 regions. Several requests show mismatched origin header and unusual UA strings.
james: logs look like replay of recently-issued JWTs, same jti but different client IPs. dumping a few lines:

```
time=2026-03-17T14:12:03Z svc=auth request_id=abcd1234 jti=71f3... user_id=5678 ip=45.32.10.5 ua="RedwoodSDK/1.3"
time=2026-03-17T14:12:04Z svc=auth request_id=abcd1235 jti=71f3... user_id=5678 ip=8.26.77.9 ua="curl/7.85"
```

anika: this smells like tokens leaked and used by a botnet. any S3 or log pushes recently?
luis: we had a staging logs sync to an external S3 host last night that was misflagged. engineering said it only contained redacted tokens but I'll confirm.
taylor: support reporting a handful of customers seeing session invalidation errors right now. no mass customer-facing incidents reported yet.
emily: pinging affected accounts to gather whether they saw suspicious auth prompts. will escalate if customers affected.
maya: immediate mitigation plan (1-4):
1) enable a temporary RPS throttle on auth endpoints (blocking bursts >200/s per jti) - @james
2) push denylist for known ASN and top offending IPs to WAF/CDN - @luis
3) enable token revocation list and start blacklisting observed jti values - @anika
4) rotate the signing key (KMS) for access tokens and roll short TTL fallback; prepare canary deploy - @james/@luis

james: starting throttle now: `kubectl apply -f auth-throttle-20260317.yaml` and adding denylist to nginx config then pushing to edges.

anika: I'll prepare revocation job. script to add jtis to redis RL is ready. running in dry-run first then flip.

luis: denylist pushed to CDN edge (rule id 9451). also blocked ASN 396982 at the edge.

pagerbot: infra-note: traffic dropped 62% after throttle + denylist. replay attempts still happening from new IPs.
maya: rotate keys ASAP — if tokens are long-lived, rotating is necessary. callout: rotating the signing key will invalidate all active tokens; prepare rollback plan.

james: initiating KMS key rotation procedure. command we run: `aws kms schedule-key-deletion --key-id alias/redwood-auth-issuing --pending-window-in-days 7` (we will use staged rollover instead of immediate deletion). I'll follow runbook.
anika: recommend instead: generate new key, sign new tokens with new key (keyless coexistance) and publish JWKS; set revocation list for observed jtis. avoids mass logout.
maya: agreed. implement key rollout with overlap window. Luis/policy: ensure verification services fetch new JWKS.

luis: deploying new JWKS to public endpoint and updating verifiers. will monitor verification error rate.

emily: notifying affected customers under the incident threshold now, telling them we may revoke active sessions and recommending password reset if they see unexpected activity.

legal: please hold off public statement until we confirm whether PII was exposed; coordinate with security for data exfil assessment.

anika: quick assessment: searching for token values in recent log exports. found ~120 entries in a staging S3 snapshot that was inadvertently made public for ~30 minutes last night. tokens were redacted in most places but raw jwt ids present in one rotated archive.

maya: ok, treat as confirmed leak of jti values. proceed with revocation + key rollout. also prepare incident summary for customers and potential breach notification timeline.

james: revocation job flipped to live. starting background job to mark jtis in RL and return 401 for revoked.

pagerbot: metric update: auth successful rate down 3% as revocations take effect; blocked traffic now concentrated on different ASN ranges.

luis: edge blocking holding. deploying secondary WAF rule to block unusual UA patterns.

anika: continuing artifact search: enumerating other S3 snapshots, cross-checking who had access. will file a full sec postmortem.

emily: drafted customer email for review - short note about precautionary session rotations and recommended reset.

maya: handoff plan: I'll stay on for the next 45m, then hand to james (overnight oncall) for monitoring. anika and luis please stay for post-rotate validation. legal to join postmortem call in 1h.

james: ACK taking overnight watch after 15:30Z. will keep slack thread updated every 30m.

legal: will prepare templated disclosure; need final count of affected accounts and evidence of PII exfiltration.

pagerbot: INCIDENT - mitigation in progress; severity: HIGH -> de-escalate to MEDIUM if no new jtis observed in 2 hours and revocation fully propagated.

maya: thanks all. quick status update at +30m. :white_check_mark:
